mainTopic: When תלמוד תורה outranks other מצוות, hidden blessings, and women's cosmetics on חול המועד
overview: This amud opens by finishing the story of the son of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, who visited רבי יונתן בן אסמאי and רבי יהודה בן גרים. The sages resolve a contradiction between two פסוקים in משלי with one rule: a מצוה others can do does not outrank learning תורה, but a מצוה only you can do does. They then bless the boy with lines that sound like curses. His father explains that each line is really a blessing: children who live, lasting marriages, long life, and a full table. A second story shows that רב's short blessing, 'do not shame and do not be shamed,' is the very blessing God gave ישראל twice. The גמרא then returns to the משנה. A woman may use cosmetics on חול המועד, and רב חסדא insists this holds at any age. רבי יהודה forbids lime unless it peels off during the מועד, and the גמרא gives two answers to show how his 'upset now, happy later' reasoning fits a משנה in עבודה זרה. The amud ends with how girls smeared their skin to remove hair, what שמן המור is, and the story of רב ביבי's daughter.

steps.title: Finishing the first answer: a מצוה only you can do
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the sages' answer to the earlier contradiction: the other פסוק is talking about a מצוה that nobody else can do for you.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the verse is talking about a מצוה that cannot be done by others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer that started just before this line. The first half covered a מצוה others can do. This half covers a מצוה that only you can do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sages explained the earlier contradiction by splitting the cases. When nobody else can do the מצוה, you should not weigh how important it is compared to your learning. You simply go and do it.

keyTerms.meaning: Here / there: points to one of the two פסוקים being compared

phrases.english: Here, it is speaking of a מצוה

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים.
phrases.english: that cannot be done by others.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּאן בְּמִצְוָה שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-part answer to the earlier contradiction between פסוקים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each פסוק refers to a different kind of מצוה
steps.terutzMaskana: A מצוה that no one else can do takes priority, and you do it right away.

steps.title: A second contradiction: can any מצוה compare to תורה?
steps.stepSummary: The sages sit again and point out that two פסוקים in משלי seem to disagree about whether 'desires of Heaven' (מצוות) can compare to תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sat again and asked: One verse says, 'She is more precious than rubies, and all YOUR desires cannot compare to her.' That suggests Heaven's desires, the מצוות, can compare to her. But another verse says, 'All desires cannot compare to her,' which means even Heaven's desires cannot compare to her!
steps.whatsHappening: The two sages start a new question. They point to two very similar פסוקים in משלי that seem to say opposite things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק says 'your desires', so only human wants fall short of תורה, and מצוות might equal it. The second פסוק drops the word 'your' and says 'all desires', which includes even מצוות. So does a מצוה compare to תורה or not?

keyTerms.meaning: They raised a question / were puzzled
Cannot be compared to her (to תורה)

steps.confusionAlert: The whole contradiction rests on one small word. The first פסוק says חֲפָצֶיךָ ('YOUR desires'), and the second says חֲפָצִים ('desires' in general). Read them side by side carefully.

phrases.english: They sat again and were asking:
It is written: 'She is more precious than rubies,'
'and all your desires cannot compare to her.'
This implies that Heaven's desires can compare to her.
And it is written: 'All desires cannot compare to her,'

phrases.aramaic: דַּאֲפִילּוּ חֶפְצֵי שָׁמַיִם לֹא יִשְׁווּ בָהּ!
phrases.english: meaning that even Heaven's desires cannot compare to her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new contradiction between פסוקים, built just like the one the sages had already resolved.
steps.kashyaTarget: How משלי 3:15 and משלי 8:11 fit together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק implies that מצוות can equal תורה, and the other implies that even מצוות cannot.

steps.title: The answer: it depends whether others can do the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: Each פסוק is talking about a different kind of מצוה. If others can do it, it does not compare to תורה. If only you can do it, it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, the verse speaks of a מצוה that others can do. There, it speaks of a מצוה that others cannot do.
steps.whatsHappening: The sages answer the contradiction with the same rule they used for the first one. One פסוק covers מצוות others can do, and the other covers מצוות only you can do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse that says 'all desires' (even מצוות) cannot compare to תורה means a מצוה others can handle. So you should not stop learning for it. The verse that says only 'your desires' fall short leaves room for a מצוה nobody else can do. For that kind of מצוה, you stop learning and do it.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule from both contradictions: if someone else can do the מצוה, keep learning תורה. If only you can do it, stop and do the מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule for practical הלכה about when a person who is learning תורה should stop to do a מצוה.

phrases.english: Here, it is speaking of a מצוה that can
phrases.notes: This 'here' is the second פסוק, 'all desires', where even מצוות do not compare.

phrases.english: be done by others;
there, it is speaking of a מצוה that cannot
phrases.notes: This 'there' is the first פסוק, 'your desires'.

phrases.english: be done by others.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּאן בְּמִצְוָה שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוקים seem to disagree about whether מצוות can compare to תורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A מצוה others can do does not outrank תורה. A מצוה only you can do does.

steps.title: The sages ask the boy why he came
steps.stepSummary: The sages notice the son of רבי שמעון בן יוחי and ask him what he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: What do you want here?
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves back to the visitor. The sages ask the son of רבי שמעון בן יוחי why he came. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the boy has quietly watched the two sages learn. Their question brings the story to the reason for his visit.

phrases.english: They said to him: What do you want here?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the learning discussion and returns to the story of the visit.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the boy came to them

steps.title: His father sent him for a blessing
steps.stepSummary: The boy explains that his father told him to go to these sages so they would bless him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: My father told me, 'Go to them so that they will bless you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The boy answers the sages' question. His father sent him to get a ברכה from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer explains the whole visit. It also prepares us for the next step, where the 'blessing' they give sounds very strange.

keyTerms.meaning: So that they will bless you

phrases.english: He said to them: Because Father told me:
Go to them so that they will bless you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His father, רבי שמעון בן יוחי, sent him to receive their ברכה.

steps.title: A blessing that sounds like a curse
steps.stepSummary: The sages bless the boy with a list of lines that, on the surface, all sound like curses.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: May it be God's will that you sow and not reap, bring in and not take out, take out and not bring in; that your house be destroyed and your lodging place be lived in; that your table be thrown into confusion; and that you not see a new year.
steps.whatsHappening: The sages give the ברכה the boy asked for. Every line of it sounds like something bad happening to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each line pairs something you want (reaping, a standing house, a new year) with a loss. As written here, the boy hears only curses. The story builds toward an explanation of what these words really mean.

keyTerms.meaning: You will sow / you will reap
You will bring in / you will take out
Your lodging place (a temporary place to stay)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not decide yet that the sages were cursing him. The words sound like curses, but his father, רבי שמעון בן יוחי, sent him for a ברכה, and the story goes on to explain these lines.

phrases.english: They said to him: May it be God's will
that you sow and not reap,
that you bring in and not take out,
that you take out and not bring in,
that your house be destroyed and your lodging place be inhabited,
that your table be thrown into confusion,
and that you not see a new year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: יְהֵא רַעֲוָא דְּתִזְרַע וְלָא תֶּחְצַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The sages respond to the boy's request for a ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sages bless the boy with phrases that on the surface sound like curses.

steps.title: The son complains that the sages hurt him instead of blessing him
steps.stepSummary: The son returns to רבי שמעון בן יוחי and says the sages did not bless him and even caused him pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came back to his father, he said: Not only did they not bless me, they even hurt me.
steps.whatsHappening: The son reports back to his father, upset. This sets up the father's question and his explanation of the blessings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken at face value, the lines from step 6 sound like curses. The son's complaint raises the problem the rest of the story will solve: were these really blessings?

keyTerms.meaning: Not only, it goes without saying

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא לְגַבֵּי אֲבוּהּ, אֲמַר לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: When he came to his father, he said to him:
Not only did they not bless me,
but they even caused me pain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The son reacts to the curse-like blessings from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The son understood the sages' words as curses.

steps.title: The father asks what the sages said
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי asks his son exactly what the sages told him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What did they say to you?
steps.whatsHappening: The father asks for the exact words before he reacts. This prepares for his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not accept his son's reading right away. He wants the actual wording so he can interpret it.

phrases.english: He said to him: What did they say to you?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the son's complaint by asking for details.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact words of the sages' blessing.

steps.title: The son repeats their words
steps.stepSummary: The son tells his father what the sages said.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said such and such to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The son repeats the lines from step 6. The גמרא does not write them out again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Such and such' is a shortcut. It points back to the full list already quoted in step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: Such and such, this and that

phrases.english: They said such and such to me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the father's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The son repeats the list of curse-like lines from step 6.

steps.title: The first three lines are really blessings about children
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says all the lines are blessings, then explains 'sow and not reap,' 'bring in and not take out,' and 'take out and not bring in.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: These are all blessings. 'Sow and not reap' means have sons who do not die. 'Bring in and not take out' means bring in brides for your sons, and your sons should not die and leave the brides widows who go away. 'Take out and not bring in' means marry off daughters, and their husbands should not die and send them back to you.
steps.whatsHappening: The father answers his son's complaint: every line is a hidden blessing. He starts decoding them one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each line sounds like loss but describes a family that stays whole. 'Not reaping' means your children are not cut down. Brides who come in stay, and daughters who go out do not come back widowed.

keyTerms.meaning: You will sow and not reap

steps.confusionAlert: 'Sow and not reap' is not about farming that fails. 'Reaping' here stands for children dying, so 'not reaping' is the blessing.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָנָךְ כּוּלְּהוּ בִּרְכָתָא נִינְהוּ.
phrases.english: He said to him: These are all blessings.
"You should sow and not reap":
you should have sons, and they should not die.
"You should bring in and not take out":
you should bring in brides
and your sons should not die, which would make them leave.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the brides. If the sons died, their widows would leave the house.

phrases.english: "You should take out and not bring in":
you should have daughters
and their husbands should not die, which would make them come back to you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the son's complaint by reinterpreting the lines.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lines are curses about loss.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lines are blessings for children who live and marriages that last.

steps.title: Your 'house' is the next world, your 'lodging' is this world
steps.stepSummary: 'Your house should be ruined and your lodging inhabited' means: stay long in this world before going to your permanent home.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Your house should be ruined and your lodging place inhabited': this world is your lodging place, and the next world is your house.
steps.whatsHappening: The father decodes the next line. He explains what 'house' and 'lodging' really stand for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This world is only a temporary inn, and the next world is the permanent house. So the blessing is that your stay in this world should go on a long time: a blessing for long life.

phrases.english: "Your house should be ruined and your lodging place should be inhabited":
for this world is your lodging place,
and that world is the house,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues decoding the list of blessings.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A curse that your home be destroyed.
steps.terutzMaskana: A blessing that you live long in this world, your temporary lodging.

steps.title: A פסוק shows the grave is a person's 'house'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'קרבם בתימו לעולם' is read as 'קברם,' their graves are their houses forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Their inner thought is that their houses last forever.' Do not read 'their inner thought' (קרבם) but 'their grave' (קברם).
steps.whatsHappening: The father brings a פסוק to prove that the permanent 'house' means the grave and the next world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By swapping two letters, 'קרבם' becomes 'קברם,' so the פסוק says their graves are their houses forever. This supports calling the next world 'the house' and this world only a 'lodging.'

phrases.english: as it is written: "Their inner thought is that their houses last forever."
Do not read "their inner thought" but "their grave."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reading of 'house' as the next world.
steps.raayaObject: That a person's permanent 'house' is the grave and the next world.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 49:12, read as קברם instead of קרבם.

steps.title: A noisy table and no 'new year' are blessings too
steps.stepSummary: 'Your table should be confused' means it should be busy with sons and daughters. 'You should not see a new year' means your wife should not die, so you never need to remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Your table should be thrown into confusion': with many sons and daughters. 'You should not see a new year': your wife should not die, so you will not marry another woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The father decodes the last two lines and finishes his answer to the son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A messy, noisy table means a big family around it. A 'new year' points to the first year of a new marriage, so never seeing one means your first marriage lasts.
steps.whatToRemember: Every line that sounded like a curse was really a blessing: children who live, lasting marriages, long life, and a full table.

phrases.english: "Your table should be thrown into confusion": with sons and daughters.
"And you should not see a new year":
phrases.notes: A newly married man has a special first year (דברים 24:5), so a 'new year' hints at a new marriage.

phrases.english: that your wife should not die
and you should not marry another woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes decoding the list of blessings.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Curses of a chaotic home and not living to see a new year.
steps.terutzMaskana: Blessings of a large family and a marriage that lasts.

steps.title: A second story: רב blesses רבי שמעון בן חלפתא
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן חלפתא takes leave of רב. His father sends him back for a blessing, and רב blesses him that he should not shame others and not be shamed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן חלפתא took leave of רב. His father told him: Go to him so he will bless you. רב said: May it be God's will that you not shame others and not be shamed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new, similar story about a short blessing whose value is not obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the first story, a father sends his son to a great teacher for a blessing. This time the blessing is short and plain, which sets up the son's reaction.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן חֲלַפְתָּא אִפְּטַר מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta took leave of Rav.
His father said to him:
Go to him so that he will bless you.
He said to him: May it be God's will
phrases.notes: The גמרא skips over him going back. Now רב is the one speaking.

phrases.english: that you should not shame others and not be shamed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן חֲלַפְתָּא אִפְּטַר מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story on the same theme of a blessing whose value is hidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב blesses him not to shame others and not to be shamed.

steps.title: The father asks what רב said
steps.stepSummary: The son comes home, and his father asks what blessing רב gave him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came to his father. His father said: What did he say to you?
steps.whatsHappening: The father asks about the blessing. This sets up the son's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the first story, where the father also asked for the exact words. It prepares for the son to judge the blessing.

phrases.english: He came to his father.
He said to him: What did he say to you?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the blessing from רב.

steps.title: The son says it was just ordinary words
steps.stepSummary: The son answers that רב only said ordinary words, nothing special.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He just said ordinary words to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The son plays down the blessing as nothing important. This sets up the father's response that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the son thinks the blessing is empty rather than a curse. Like the first story, the reader expects to learn that this simple-sounding blessing is really valuable.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִילִּין בְּעָלְמָא הוּא דְּאָמַר לִי.
phrases.english: He said to him: He just said ordinary words to me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the father's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The son thinks רב's blessing was ordinary and of little value.

steps.title: The father proves רב's blessing was a great one
steps.stepSummary: The father tells his son that 'not to shame and not be shamed' is the very blessing הקדוש ברוך הוא gave ישראל, and it appears twice in a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The father said: He blessed you with the blessing הקדוש ברוך הוא gave ישראל, and He even said it twice, as it says: 'You will eat and be satisfied and praise... and My people will never be ashamed. And you will know that I am among ישראל... and My people will never be ashamed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The son thought רב's blessing was plain, so the father proves from a פסוק that it is a huge blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son judged the blessing by its simple wording. The father shows that the same words, 'never be ashamed,' are God's own promise to ישראל. Because the פסוק repeats them twice in a row, it is clearly a special blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: And repeated it (said it a second time)

steps.whatToRemember: Not being shamed is not a small wish. It is the blessing God Himself gave ישראל, and He said it twice.

phrases.english: He said to him: He blessed you with the blessing
with which the Holy One, Blessed be He, blessed Israel
and He repeated it, as it is written:
"And you shall eat in plenty and be satisfied
and you shall praise, etc.
and My people shall never be ashamed.

phrases.aramaic: וִידַעְתֶּם כִּי בְקֶרֶב יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲנִי וְגוֹ׳
phrases.english: And you shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, etc.
and My people shall never be ashamed."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בָּרְכָךְ בִּרְכְּתָא דְּבֵרְכָן קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the son's claim in step 16 that רב said only ordinary words.
steps.raayaObject: That 'not shaming and not being shamed' is a great blessing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יואל 2:26–27, where 'My people shall never be ashamed' is said twice.

steps.title: Which cosmetic treatments a woman may do on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה allowing a woman's cosmetics on חול המועד, and a ברייתא lists them: eye paint, hair removal, rouge; some add removing hair from the lower body.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said a woman may do her beauty treatments. The Rabbis taught: these are women's beauty treatments: painting her eyes, removing hair, and putting rouge on her face. Some say: also removing hair from her lower body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a new line of the משנה and explains it with a ברייתא that lists the allowed beauty treatments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said 'her cosmetics' in general. The ברייתא fills in what that means with concrete examples. A second opinion adds one more item to the list.

keyTerms.meaning: She paints her eyes with eye-paint (כחל)
Rouge (in the second opinion: a comb)

phrases.english: "And a woman may do her cosmetic treatments."
The Rabbis taught:
These are the cosmetic treatments of women:
She paints her eyes and removes unwanted hair
and puts rouge on her face.
And some say:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲבֶרֶת סְרָק עַל פָּנֶיהָ שֶׁל מַטָּה.
phrases.english: she may pass a comb over her lower "face."
phrases.notes: A modest way of saying she may remove hair from her private area.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story of רב's blessing and returns to the משנה's laws of חול המועד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On חול המועד a woman may paint her eyes, remove hair, and apply rouge; some also allow removing hair from the lower body.

steps.title: רב הונא בר חיננא limits the rule to young women
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא's wife, already a mother-in-law, adorned herself on חול המועד. רב הונא בר חיננא said the permission is only for a young woman, not an old one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא's wife would make herself pretty in front of her daughter-in-law. רב הונא בר חיננא was sitting before רב חסדא and said: The rule was taught only about a young woman, but not about an old woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about an older woman using cosmetics, and a scholar suggests the משנה's permission doesn't cover older women. This sets up רב חסדא's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא בר חיננא reasons that beauty treatments are allowed because they bring joy, so they fit a young woman. An older woman, he thinks, doesn't need them, so the permission shouldn't apply. His remark is aimed at what רב חסדא's own wife was doing.

keyTerms.meaning: A young woman / an old woman

phrases.english: Rav Chisda's wife
would adorn herself in front of her daughter-in-law.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Chinnana was sitting before Rav Chisda
and he sat and said:
They taught this only about a young woman,
but an old woman, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא יַלְדָּה, אֲבָל זְקֵנָה — לֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a limit on the permission given in the משנה and ברייתא of step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא בר חיננא: only a young woman may do cosmetics on חול המועד, not an old woman.

steps.title: רב חסדא insists the rule includes even very old women
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא swears that the permission covers even רב הונא בר חיננא's own mother and grandmother, and even a woman at the edge of her grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: By God! Even your mother, even your grandmother, and even a woman standing at the edge of her grave may adorn herself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא strongly rejects the idea that older women are left out of the permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא בר חיננא had cut the rule down to young women. רב חסדא removes that limit completely, using the most extreme examples: even a woman about to die. So age makes no difference at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing at her grave, meaning extremely old

phrases.english: He said to him: By God!
Even your mother, and even your mother's mother,
and even one standing at the edge of her grave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects the limit proposed in step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that only young women may use cosmetics on חול המועד.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly assumes older women get no joy from adorning themselves.

steps.title: A popular saying: women of all ages love to look nice
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא supports his view with a folk saying: a woman of sixty runs to the sound of the drum just like a girl of six.
steps.simpleTranslation: As people say: A woman of sixty, like a girl of six, runs when she hears the drum.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא backs up his rejection with a well-known saying from everyday life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying shows that older women stay young at heart and enjoy celebration like little girls. Since beauty treatments give them joy too, the reason for the permission applies to them as well.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows the reason: cosmetics on חול המועד are allowed because they bring a woman joy, and that is true at every age.

phrases.english: As people say:
A woman of sixty, like a girl of six,
runs to the sound of the drum.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי: בַּת שִׁיתִּין כְּבַת שֵׁית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רב חסדא's rejection in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That older women also enjoy adornment, so they too may use cosmetics on חול המועד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A popular saying: 'A woman of sixty, like a girl of six, runs to the sound of the drum.'

steps.title: רבי יהודה forbids lime but allows lime that peels off during the holiday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה from the משנה: a woman may not apply lime. A ברייתא explains that it makes her look bad. He agrees she may use lime that will peel off within the מועד, because she will be happy afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says she may not apply lime. A ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says a woman may not apply lime because it makes her look ugly. But he agrees that lime she can peel off during the מועד may be applied during the מועד. Even though she is upset now, she will be happy later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רבי יהודה's opinion in the משנה. It brings a ברייתא that gives his reason and a limit to his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's concern is that lime makes the woman look bad, so she would be unhappy on the יום טוב. If the lime comes off while the מועד is still going on, she gets to enjoy the result during the holiday. So the short-term upset is outweighed by the joy that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Apply lime (סיד) to the skin, used to remove hair or improve the skin
Disgrace, an ugly or unattractive appearance

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the principle 'distressed now, happy later'. The next step will test whether רבי יהודה really holds it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: She may not apply lime.
It is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehuda says:
A woman may not apply lime
because it is a disgrace to her.
But Rabbi Yehuda agrees regarding lime
that she can peel off during the Festival,
that she may smear it on during the Festival.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּצֵירָה הִיא עַכְשָׁיו —
phrases.english: For even though she is distressed now,
she is happy afterward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story of רב חסדא and goes back to the משנה, now to explain רבי יהודה's dissenting opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lime that leaves the woman looking bad through the holiday is forbidden. Lime that peels off during the מועד is allowed, because she will be happy afterward.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה really accept 'distressed now, happy later'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from a משנה in עבודה זרה. There, רבי יהודה allows collecting a debt from idolaters before their holiday because they are upset when they pay. The חכמים answered that they will be happy later, and רבי יהודה did not accept that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really hold this reasoning? We learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה says one may collect a debt from them because the payer is upset. The חכמים said to him: even though he is upset now, he will be happy later!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that is really a challenge. It points to a משנה where רבי יהודה seems to reject the very reasoning the ברייתא gave in his name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In עבודה זרה, the חכמים are the ones who say 'he is upset now but happy later'. רבי יהודה looks only at the present upset. That clashes with the ברייתא, where רבי יהודה himself relies on 'happy later' to allow the peelable lime.

keyTerms.meaning: One collects payment of a debt

steps.confusionAlert: In the עבודה זרה case we do NOT want the idolater to be happy, because he might thank his idol. So 'happy later' is a reason to forbid there. Here it is a reason to permit. Either way, the question is only whether רבי יהודה takes the later happiness into account at all.

phrases.english: But does Rabbi Yehuda hold
this reasoning?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:
Rabbi Yehuda says: One may collect a debt from them
because he is distressed.
They said to him:
Even though he is distressed now,
he is happy afterward!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַאי סְבָרָא? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning the ברייתא gave in רבי יהודה's name.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that רבי יהודה permits peelable lime because 'she is happy afterward'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה in עבודה זרה, רבי יהודה ignores later happiness and looks only at present distress. The 'happy later' argument belongs to the חכמים he disagrees with.

steps.title: The laws of the מועד are a special case
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the laws of the מועד are different. Everything permitted on the מועד is permitted because it is trouble now and joy later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Leave aside the laws of the מועד. All of them work as 'upset now, happy later'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק resolves the contradiction. רבי יהודה uses the 'happy later' reasoning only for the laws of the מועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole system of מועד permissions, like cooking and preparing food, involves effort now for enjoyment afterward. So even רבי יהודה must accept this reasoning for the מועד. That does not mean he accepts it in other areas, such as debts in עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave aside, set apart as a separate case

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה ignores later happiness in general, as in the debt case in עבודה זרה. For the laws of the מועד he accepts 'upset now, happy later', because that is how all the מועד permissions work.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Leave aside the laws of the Festival,
for all of them are 'distressed now'
and 'happy afterward'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: הַנַּח לְהִלְכוֹת מוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by limiting רבי יהודה's use of 'happy later' to the laws of the מועד.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between areas of law: the laws of the מועד versus other areas.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה rejects 'happy later' everywhere, so the ברייתא contradicts the משנה in עבודה זרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The laws of the מועד are built on 'trouble now, joy later', so רבי יהודה accepts the reasoning there even though he rejects it for debts.

steps.title: רבינא: a gentile is never happy about paying
steps.stepSummary: רבינא gives a different answer to the contradiction in רבי יהודה. A גוי who pays a debt is always upset, so there is no 'joy later' for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: When it comes to paying back a debt, a גוי is always upset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the contradiction from step 23. רבינא says the debt case is different because a גוי never becomes happy about money he paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר יצחק answered that the laws of the מועד are a special case. רבינא answers from the other side: רבי יהודה does accept 'trouble now, joy later' in general. In the debt case the later joy simply never comes, because the גוי stays upset about his lost money forever.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew; here, the idolater who repays the loan

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the contradiction. רב נחמן בר יצחק says the מועד is special. רבינא says the גוי never becomes happy, so the debt case is different.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
A gentile, regarding repaying a debt,
is always distressed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: גּוֹי לְעִנְיַן פֵּרָעוֹן לְעוֹלָם מֵצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer, alongside רב נחמן בר יצחק's, to the same contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case on its facts: in the debt case, the later joy never actually happens.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה seems to reject the 'joy later' idea everywhere, which would contradict the ברייתא about lime.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה accepts 'joy later' in general. A גוי repaying a debt never feels it, so the two rulings do not clash.

steps.title: How young girls smeared their bodies: lime, flour, or oil
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says that girls who matured physically before reaching the age of adulthood smeared themselves: poor girls with lime, rich girls with fine flour, and princesses with שמן המור, as the פסוק in אסתר says.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Jewish girls who had matured physically but had not yet reached the years of adulthood: the poor ones smeared themselves with lime, the rich ones with fine flour, and daughters of kings with שמן המור, as it says, 'Six months with שמן המור.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic connected to the lime (סיד) in the משנה. רב יהודה describes what different girls smeared on their bodies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that smearing lime on the body was a known practice, and a cheap one. Richer families used finer materials. The proof that princesses used שמן המור comes from the women prepared for King אחשורוש in מגילת אסתר. The ברייתא in step 29 shows that this oil removes hair, which suggests the smearing was done for the same purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: A special oil (defined in the next steps)

steps.confusionAlert: This is רב יהודה, an אמורא. He is a different person from רבי יהודה, the תנא in the משנה who forbids applying lime on the מועד.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Daughters of Israel who reached their maturity
but did not yet reach the years,
phrases.notes: He means girls whose bodies matured before they reached the age of adulthood.

phrases.english: the poor ones smear them with lime,
the rich ones smear them with fine flour,
daughters of kings with shemen hamor,
as it is stated:
"Six months with shemen hamor."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהִגִּיעוּ לְפִירְקָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the debt discussion and returns to the topic of lime from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Poor girls used lime, rich girls fine flour, and princesses שמן המור, based on אסתר 2:12.

steps.title: What is שמן המור?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the oil mentioned in the פסוק actually is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is שמן המור?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the unusual term שמן המור. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase comes from the פסוק that רב יהודה quoted, but it is not clear what substance it means. The גמרא asks so the term can be defined.

phrases.english: What is "shemen hamor"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a term from the פסוק quoted in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the substance called שמן המור.

steps.title: Two definitions: a perfume or unripe olive oil
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חייא says שמן המור is סטכת, a kind of perfume. רב ירמיה בר אמי says it is olive oil from olives that have not reached a third of their growth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חייא said: It is סטכת. רב ירמיה בר אמי said: It is olive oil from olives that have not reached one-third of their growth.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question, and each gives a different definition of שמן המור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One opinion says it is a perfume called סטכת. The other says it is oil from very unripe olives. The next step brings a ברייתא that supports the second definition.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Ḥiyya said:
setaket,
phrases.notes: This is the name of a kind of perfume.

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Ami said:
olive oil that has not reached one-third.
phrases.notes: He means the oil comes from olives that are still less than a third grown.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר: סְטָכַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either the perfume סטכת, or oil from olives less than a third grown.

steps.title: A ברייתא: אנפיקינון is unripe olive oil that removes hair
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה: אנפיקינון is oil from olives that have not reached a third of their growth. It is smeared on the body because it removes hair and softens the skin.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה says, אנפיקינון is olive oil from olives that have not reached one-third of their growth. Why do people smear it on? Because it removes hair and makes the skin soft.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that describes the same oil רב ירמיה בר אמי mentioned. The ברייתא also explains why it is used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the same definition as רב ירמיה בר אמי, so it supports his view. It also explains the use: the oil removes hair and softens the skin. That fits what the princesses in step 26 were doing.
steps.whatToRemember: שמן המור, according to רב ירמיה בר אמי and supported by the ברייתא, is oil from unripe olives. It removes hair and softens the skin.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Anpikinon is olive oil
that has not reached one-third.
And why do they smear it on?
Because it removes the hair
and softens the skin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that matches רב ירמיה בר אמי's definition.
steps.raayaObject: רב ירמיה בר אמי's definition: oil from olives less than a third grown.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in the name of רבי יהודה defining אנפיקינון the same way.

steps.title: רב ביבי smears his daughter limb by limb
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי smeared his daughter one limb at a time. She became so beautiful that he received four hundred זוז for her when she married.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי had a daughter. He smeared her one limb at a time, and he received four hundred זוז for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing the smearing from the earlier steps being done in real life. It is also setting up the story of the neighbor that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that this smearing removes hair and softens the skin. Here we see that it worked when done slowly, one part of the body at a time. The high price he received shows how well it worked.

keyTerms.meaning: He smeared her (with a substance on the skin)
Limb by limb, one part of the body at a time
זוז coins, a common silver coin

phrases.english: Rav Beivai had a daughter,
he smeared her limb by limb.
He took four hundred zuz for her.
phrases.notes: He means when she got married. She had become so attractive that a large amount was paid for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the hair-removing smearing from step 29 being used in a real story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Careful smearing, one limb at a time, made רב ביבי's daughter very beautiful.

steps.title: The gentile neighbor copies him and his daughter dies
steps.stepSummary: A גוי neighbor smeared his own daughter's whole body all at once, and she died. He blamed רב ביבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain גוי lived in רב ביבי's neighborhood, and he also had a daughter. He smeared her whole body at one time, and she died. He said: ביבי killed my daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. A neighbor copies רב ביבי but does it the wrong way, all at once, and his daughter dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference between the two stories is how the smearing was done: limb by limb, or the whole body at once. Done all at once, it was deadly. The גוי blamed רב ביבי because he was the one being copied.
steps.confusionAlert: רב ביבי did nothing wrong. The neighbor's daughter died because of how her father did the smearing (all at once), not because of anything רב ביבי did.

phrases.english: There was a certain gentile in his neighborhood
who had a daughter.
He smeared her all at once, and she died.
He said: Beivai killed my daughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story by showing what happened when the smearing was done all at once instead of limb by limb.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Smearing the whole body at one time was deadly.

steps.title: רב נחמן: only beer drinkers' daughters need smearing
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says that רב ביבי's daughters needed smearing because his household drank beer. Those who do not drink beer do not need it for their daughters.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: רב ביבי drinks beer, so his daughters need smearing. We do not drink beer, so our daughters do not need smearing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן comments on the story and limits the need for this treatment to households like רב ביבי's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן links the need for smearing to drinking beer. The idea seems to be that beer brings more body hair, so beer drinkers' daughters need the hair removed. Families who don't drink beer have no reason to use this treatment, which the story just showed can be dangerous.
steps.whatToRemember: רב ביבי's careful smearing worked, while smearing all at once killed the neighbor's daughter. רב נחמן teaches that this treatment was only needed in beer-drinking homes, not in his.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Rav Beivai, who drinks beer,
his daughters need smearing,
we, who do not drink beer,
our daughters do not need smearing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: רַב בִּיבִי דְּשָׁתֵי שִׁיכְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the story and explains why רב ביבי needed the smearing while others do not.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Smearing is needed only for the daughters of beer drinkers. Those who do not drink beer do not need it.
